migration.headline: RSA → ML-KEM-768: 2 system(s) — 0 blocked, 2 need a parallel run, 0 can migrate directly. Recommended: parallel migration

strategy.meaning: run the old and the new algorithm side by side, then retire the old one

parallel_mechanisms.how: offer a hybrid group (classical + ML-KEM-768, e.g. X25519MLKEM768) on TLS 1.3: upgraded peers negotiate it, the rest fall back to the classical group
serve both the RSA and the ML-KEM-768 chain (or a composite certificate) until every relying party trusts the new root
make the algorithm a per-connection setting so each peer and vendor moves on its own date and can be rolled back alone

strategy.direct_is_safe_when: no connected system outside the change, no network endpoint with unseen clients, no vendor, no stored data or signatures under the old algorithm, and every device's capability is recorded

twin_context.source: Live estate graph — the agents' observations (systems from the bank-approved mapping, hosts, services, libraries, listening endpoints and their negotiated TLS, certificates, HSMs, platform servers, vendors and their contracts, declared and observed system connections)

findings.title: Core Banking is connected to Branch Banking but is not part of this change
findings.detail: Branch Banking calls Core Banking; its crypto is not recorded in the twin, so its support for ML-KEM-768 is unknown
findings.subject: Core Banking
findings.mitigation: keep RSA available on this connection until Core Banking confirms ML-KEM-768, then retire it
findings.if_ignored: the connection between Branch Banking and Core Banking fails its handshake or signature check at cut-over

findings.title: 10.210.0.5:443 negotiates TLS TLSv1
findings.detail: post-quantum and hybrid key exchange (ML-KEM-768) is only defined for TLS 1.3
findings.mitigation: enable TLS 1.3 on this endpoint (and its load balancer) first
findings.if_ignored: the endpoint can never offer the new key exchange

findings.title: 1 RSA certificate(s) to reissue
findings.mitigation: confirm the issuing CA can sign with the new algorithm, issue the new certificates, and distribute the new chain to every relying party before switching
findings.if_ignored: relying parties that do not trust the new chain reject the connection

findings.title: larger keys and signatures on 1 endpoint(s)
findings.detail: ML-KEM-768 keys/ciphertexts/signatures are much larger than RSA's; handshakes grow by kilobytes
findings.mitigation: test through every load balancer, WAF and TLS-inspecting middlebox on the path; check MTU/fragmentation and constrained clients
findings.if_ignored: middleboxes that cap ClientHello size drop the new handshakes

plan.title: Clear what stops the migration
actions: library OpenSSL 3.3.2 does not implement ML-KEM-768 — upgrade to a version (or add a provider) that implements ML-KEM-768, then rebuild and redeploy
10.210.0.5:443 negotiates TLS TLSv1 — enable TLS 1.3 on this endpoint (and its load balancer) first
Alpine Linux: ML-KEM-768 support is not recorded — ask the vendor for its supported-algorithm statement and add it to the vendor crypto inventory
plan.exit_criteria: every blocker is closed with evidence (capability list, vendor statement, release) and recorded in the twin
plan.rollback: nothing to roll back — no production change yet

plan.title: Prepare ML-KEM-768 keys and trust
actions: generate ML-KEM-768 keys for Branch Banking
generate ML-KEM-768 keys for SWIFT Gateway
issue ML-KEM-768 certificates for Branch Banking, SWIFT Gateway and distribute the new trust anchors to relying parties
plan.exit_criteria: new keys exist where the system will use them; relying parties trust the new chain
plan.rollback: unused keys and certificates are revoked; nothing is serving them yet

plan.title: Wave 1: enable ML-KEM-768 next to RSA
actions: Branch Banking: accept and offer ML-KEM-768 while still accepting RSA
SWIFT Gateway: accept and offer ML-KEM-768 while still accepting RSA
plan.exit_criteria: both algorithms negotiate; monitoring shows which peers use which
plan.rollback: switch ML-KEM-768 off again — RSA never stopped working

plan.title: Wave 1: move to ML-KEM-768
actions: Branch Banking: prefer ML-KEM-768; move each connected peer and vendor once it confirms
SWIFT Gateway: prefer ML-KEM-768; move each connected peer and vendor once it confirms
plan.exit_criteria: handshakes, signatures and business transactions succeed on the new algorithm for every listed system
plan.rollback: re-enable RSA on the affected connections
plan.providers_first: systems that others call move before their callers

plan.title: Verify on the twin and in production
actions: re-scan the changed systems so the twin shows the new algorithm
run each business process's smoke test
confirm no connection still negotiates RSA
plan.exit_criteria: the twin no longer reports RSA on these systems

plan.title: Retire RSA
actions: disable RSA once every peer and vendor has confirmed ML-KEM-768
keep RSA verification until old signatures expire
plan.exit_criteria: no system, peer or vendor depends on RSA
plan.rollback: re-enable RSA (keys are destroyed only after a holding period)

unknowns: which algorithm each connection negotiates is not recorded on dependency edges; a connected system is treated as needing the old algorithm until it confirms
clients of a network endpoint are not assets in the twin, so they cannot be checked
hardware and vendor capability is as recorded or declared — not independently tested
performance of the new algorithm on this estate is not measured here
1 twin asset(s) and 1 evidence record(s) use RSA but are linked to no system, so they are not in any wave
Branch Banking: no crypto↔hardware link is recorded, so whether its keys live in an HSM (and whether that HSM can run the target) is unknown
SWIFT Gateway: no crypto↔hardware link is recorded, so whether its keys live in an HSM (and whether that HSM can run the target) is unknown
